The square root of 2 is an irrational nu.why: One of the most often stated facts of mathematics, the textbook example of an irrational number, with a proof every course repeats. Thousands of exact mentions in Dolma across its spellings. It is provable, but a model meets it as a stated fact far more often than it could work it out.

notes: Delete of replace-0002's original fact. Mathematics leaves out worlds: a fact about a number or a class of numbers rests on definitions and proofs, so no premise can give way and the edit leaves no consistent world to split between (README, Shape per topic). Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. Every derived query goes through the deleted fact and expects 'does not know'. The commensurability query has a second route in the Pythagorean form of the fact ('the diagonal of a square is incommensurable with its side'), but that is the same proposition, so a delete that leaves it has not removed the fact; a model answering 'no' there re-derived what was deleted. The fourth derived query asks the continued fraction through the class (instance_of ∘ subclass_of ⊑ instance_of); the conjunction that used to be there is now the propositional 'and' query, rephrased around the original value (irrational).
